is a note for the people reading the program. It starts with two slashes,
, and ends where the line ends. It can take a whole line or go at the end of an instruction.

blocks.description: Two program lines. In the first, what follows the two slashes is shaded and labelled comment. In the second, the two slashes are inside a quoted text and are labelled ordinary text.

caption.text: Whatever is to the right of the two slashes is a comment up to the end of the line. Inside a quoted text, the slashes are just characters.

runs.text: The engine does not run comments, but it does not throw them away either: it keeps them so that the editor, the formatter and the profile translator leave them intact.
PseudoLearn only has line comments. There is no comment that opens on one line and closes on another: to comment several lines, each one gets its own

points.text: opens a comment up to the end of the line.
Comments are kept when formatting and translating.
